$comment: mapping.json — the spine of the V1 -> V3 data migration (Part 3 §2/§4).
Read by:
backend/scripts/migration/extract.mjs           Stage 1 — what to pull into v1_staging
backend/scripts/migration/lib.ts                Stage 2 — the transform runner
backend/database/scripts/verify-migration.mjs   Gate 2 — the six parity checks
TWO LAYERS, deliberately separate:
`tables`   the DISPOSITION LEDGER. Every one of the 199 tables in v1-tables.json is
dispositioned exactly once as `transform` | `drop` | `blocked`. There is no
default: an undispositioned table is an error, not a pass. This is what makes
coverage arithmetic (source rows = target rows + reason-coded skips) possible.
Coverage is arithmetic, not memory.
`mappings` the VERIFICATION DETAIL for tables already dispositioned `transform` AND already
loaded. A `transform` table with no mapping entry is honest — it says the wave has
not run yet. A mapping entry whose table is not dispositioned `transform` is a
contradiction and --self-check rejects it.
Disposition vocabulary:
transform  V1 rows become V3 rows. `targets` names the V3 table(s); `wave` names when.
drop       V1 rows are deliberately NOT carried. Needs `reasonCode` (closed enum) + `reason`.
blocked    would transform, but the V3 target does not exist yet. Needs `dependency`.
Per Part 3 §4 W7: a blocked mapping flips to `transform` the moment its target
schema merges. `blocked` is never a resting state for a shipped feature.
`question` on a blocked entry means the disposition could not be derived from the master
document plus the data. It is an open question for the owner, not a guess. Grep for it.

reasonCodes.$comment: CLOSED ENUM. Gate 2 check 6: every row in mig.unresolved and every `drop` carries one of these. An unknown reason is a red gate, because 'unexplained' is how silent data loss looks in a report.
reasonCodes.ci_junk: CI / smoke-test output. Never was product data.
reasonCodes.rebuild_in_v3: Feature is deliberately rebuilt in V3; the V1 rows are not carried (owner decision).
reasonCodes.v1_infrastructure: V1 platform plumbing that V3 replaces with its own native mechanism.
reasonCodes.secret_material: Credentials, tokens or key audit. Must never be copied into V3.
reasonCodes.ephemeral: Short-lived state with no meaning after the cutover window.
reasonCodes.v3_table_live: The V3 table exists and is already written by V3 code; loading V1 rows would corrupt live state.
reasonCodes.unresolved_user: No platform_users row for this V1 user reference.
reasonCodes.unresolved_business: No businesses row for this V1 business reference.
reasonCodes.unresolved_institution: No institutions row for this V1 institution reference.
reasonCodes.unresolved_country: Country string did not resolve to a countries row.
reasonCodes.unresolved_city: City did not resolve to a cities row for its country.
reasonCodes.unresolved_parent: A declared parent row is missing, so the child cannot be attached.
reasonCodes.duplicate_natural_key: Two source rows collapse onto one natural key; the later one is reported, not overwritten silently.
reasonCodes.invalid_source_data: Source row fails a validity rule the V3 schema enforces.

$comment: W7 LOADER CONSTRAINT, established by C1 (business/20260816_001_business_services.ts).
{tenant}.business_services.id is a UUID — the thin table's internal serial was dropped and
its `uuid` column renamed to `id`, because the uuid was already the external identity
(schema_field_values.entity_id, the master cross-tenant tables and every child/junction all
key on it). `v1_id` is a SEPARATE nullable-unique column: the loader's idempotency key.
So the Stage-2 transform writes V1's business_services.id into `v1_id`, NEVER into `id`, and
every child and junction resolves its parent through v1_id -> id. Writing the V1 uuid into
`id` would look right and quietly fuse two different identities. Tables carrying this rule
are marked idStrategy: "v1_id".

lookups.$comment: Value transforms that need a table from the OTHER database. The verifier runs `query` against `from`, materialises the rows as a VALUES CTE named after the key, and prepends it to every query on `injectInto`. This is how a free-text V1 country is compared against a V3 country_id without either side guessing.

globaly_countries.query: SELECT DISTINCT ON (key) key, id FROM (SELECT lower(btrim(name)) AS key, id, 1 AS pri FROM public.countries WHERE name IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT lower(btrim(iso2)), id, 2 FROM public.countries WHERE iso2 IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT lower(btrim(iso3)), id, 3 FROM public.countries WHERE iso3 IS NOT NULL) s WHERE key <> '' ORDER BY key, id, pri
globaly_countries.$note: Mirrors buildCountryResolver() in recon-v2-users.mjs exactly: name/iso2/iso3 all resolve, lowercased + trimmed, first writer wins (earlier country row, then name > iso2 > iso3).

globaly_issuing_orgs.query: SELECT DISTINCT ON (key) lower(btrim(name)) AS key, id FROM public.issuing_organizations WHERE name IS NOT NULL AND btrim(name) <> '' ORDER BY key, id

globaly_business_categories.query: SELECT DISTINCT ON (key) lower(btrim(slug)) AS key, id FROM public.business_categories WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND slug IS NOT NULL AND btrim(slug) <> '' ORDER BY key, id
globaly_business_categories.$note: Mirrors the uuid -> serial remap import-v1-businesses.ts does: V1 business_category_id uuid -> V1 business_categories.slug -> V3 business_categories.id.
